definitionEn: an unusual object, place or fact that attracts people's interest
senseNote: Здесь — «диковинка, необычный предмет» (a curiosity); базовое значение «любопытство, желание узнать» не рассматривается.
situation: A shop, museum or collection contains a strange or rare object that people find interesting to look at.

examples.text: The museum's basement is full of scientific [[curiosities]] collected over two centuries.
The old lock is now more of a tourist [[curiosity]] than a working part of the canal.
For collectors, a stamp with a printing error can become a valuable [[curiosity]].

texts: The lighthouse keeper's diary now sits in the museum as a local [[curiosity]].
Half-buried in the sand, the old shipwreck has become a strange [[curiosity]] for divers.
The antique shop sold the two-headed coin simply as a [[curiosity]].

badCollocation.text: we visited all the [[curiosities]] of Paris
badCollocation.noteRu: «Достопримечательности» города — sights или attractions, а не curiosities. Curiosity — редкая, необычная вещь, а не главная достопримечательность.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Магазин необычных вещей — a curiosity shop, устойчивое сочетание (как «Лавка древностей» у Диккенса). Rarity, peculiarity и eccentricity с shop так не говорят.

nuance.text: Even today, the two-headed calf preserved in formaldehyde remains a scientific [[curiosity]].
nuance.explanationRu: Curiosity — редкая, необычная вещь, интересная сама по себе, даже если её видели уже много раз. Novelty — вещь, ценная именно новизной; заспиртованный экспонат явно не «новинка».

reverse.text: The shop's front window was full of clever new [[novelties]] for the holiday season.
reverse.explanationRu: Novelty — вещь, привлекающая именно новизной, например к празднику. Curiosities — необычные, а не обязательно новые вещи; сезонные товары так не назовут.

fixIt.text: After the auction, the diamond-studded pocket watch remains a real [[interest]] among collectors.
fixIt.explanationRu: Interest — само чувство интереса, а не предмет. Необычная вещь, которая его вызывает, — a curiosity.

wordFormation.text: The museum keeper eagerly showed us every strange [[curiosity]] in the collection.

reply.context: A friend texts a photo: "Found this weird two-headed coin at the flea market, what is it?"
options: No idea, but it looks like a genuine curiosity — maybe show it to a collector.
Wow, your curiosity about old coins is amazing, you should study economics.
One's fascination with such an artefact shall no doubt prove most rewarding, dear friend.
reply.explanationRu: Curiosity здесь — необычная вещица, а не «любопытство», как во втором варианте. Третий ответ звучит слишком старомодно и напыщенно для сообщения другу.

definitionEn: the legal right and responsibility to take care of a child, especially after the parents separate
senseNote: Здесь — «опека над ребёнком» после развода; значение «содержание под стражей» (police custody) не рассматривается.
situation: After a couple separates, a court decides which parent will officially look after their children day to day.

examples.text: After a bitter divorce, she was granted full [[custody]] of the children.
The couple are still fighting over [[custody]] of their two young children.
Under the new agreement, the parents will share joint [[custody]] of their daughter.

texts: The judge awarded [[custody]] to the mother, with generous visiting rights for the father.
Many fathers say the courts still favour mothers when deciding [[custody]].
Losing [[custody]] of her son was the hardest moment of her life.

badCollocation.text: fight for the [[custody]] of their son
badCollocation.noteRu: Custody — неисчисляемое существительное, лишний артикль the не нужен: fight for custody of their son (без the перед custody).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Sole custody — единоличная опека, устойчивое сочетание. Ownership, citizenship и membership с опекой над ребёнком не связаны.

nuance.text: The couple's long divorce battle ended with the mother getting full [[custody]] of the children.
nuance.explanationRu: Custody — родитель заботится о ребёнке после развода. Guardianship — когда опекуном становится не родитель, обычно из-за смерти или недееспособности родителей; к разводу это слово не подходит.

reverse.text: When both parents died in the accident, the children's grandmother was granted legal [[guardianship]].
reverse.explanationRu: Опекунство после смерти обоих родителей — guardianship. Custody — обычно про решение между родителями, а их здесь уже нет.

fixIt.text: After the divorce, the father won [[guardianship]] of his two sons and sees them every weekend.
fixIt.explanationRu: После развода термин — custody (родитель получает опеку по суду). Guardianship используется, когда опекуном становится не родитель.

wordFormation.text: As the [[custodial]] parent, she makes most day-to-day decisions about their son's schooling.

reply.context: A friend confides: "The custody hearing is next week and I'm terrified I'll lose."
options: Try to stay calm — most judges decide custody based on what's best for the kids, not who shouts loudest.
Don't worry, you'll definitely get custody of the house and the car too.
One trusts that the judiciary shall rule with utmost impartiality regarding said custody of the children.
reply.explanationRu: Custody — про заботу о детях после развода; про дом и машину так не говорят (ошибка во втором варианте). Третий звучит как судебный протокол, а не слова друга.

rewrite.original: A court decided that the children would live mainly with their mother after the divorce.

definitionEn: a short piece cut out of a newspaper or magazine and kept for reference
senseNote: Здесь — «вырезка» из газеты или журнала; значения «черенок растения» и «выемка в грунте под дорогу» не рассматриваются.
situation: Someone keeps a small piece cut from a newspaper or magazine because the article or photo interests them.

examples.text: My grandmother kept every newspaper [[cutting]] that mentioned our family.
The reporter pinned old press [[cuttings]] about the scandal to the wall behind her desk.
He found a yellowing [[cutting]] about his father's wedding inside the old book.

texts: She keeps a folder of [[cuttings]] about local history.
The library stores old [[cuttings]] from wartime newspapers.
He still has [[cuttings]] praising his first novel.

badCollocation.noteRu: Газетную вырезку не «делают» (make): её cut out (вырезают) или keep (хранят). Make a cutting так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Вырезки из газеты — newspaper cuttings (или clippings). Stamps, tickets и labels с newspaper так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: She kept a yellowing [[cutting]] about the wedding inside her old diary.
nuance.explanationRu: Cutting — вырезанный из газеты кусок бумаги, физический объект. Excerpt — отрывок из текста (книги, речи), необязательно вырезанный ножницами.

reverse.text: The teacher read a short [[excerpt]] from the novel's opening chapter.
reverse.explanationRu: Отрывок из книги — excerpt, его не вырезают ножницами. Cutting — именно вырезанный из газеты или журнала кусок бумаги.

fixIt.text: She keeps a small [[excerpt]] from the wedding announcement in her wallet.
fixIt.explanationRu: Вырезанный из газеты кусок бумаги — cutting, а не excerpt (excerpt — отрывок текста, а не вырезанный листок).

wordFormation.text: My aunt kept an old newspaper [[cutting]] about her wedding day.

definitionEn: believing that people only act for selfish reasons, not sincere ones
situation: You assume that people's kind words or good actions are really driven by self-interest rather than honesty.

examples.text: After years in politics, she has become deeply [[cynical]] about campaign promises.
It's hard not to feel [[cynical]] when yet another politician breaks a promise.
My [[cynical]] side wonders if the charity event is really about publicity.

texts: Don't be so [[cynical]] — maybe he really did mean to help.
Years of office politics had left her thoroughly [[cynical]].
The article takes a [[cynical]] view of modern celebrity culture.

badCollocation.text: he made a [[cynical]] joke about my new haircut
badCollocation.noteRu: Насмешливую, язвительную шутку называют sarcastic. Cynical — о недоверии к чужим мотивам, а не о мелкой насмешке.

collocationTask.prompt: The article takes a ___ view of politics, assuming that every politician lies.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Cynical view — взгляд, исходящий из недоверия к мотивам людей. Curious, generous и athletic по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: He's deeply [[cynical]] about politicians — he assumes they are all corrupt and self-serving.
nuance.explanationRu: Cynical — не верит в искренние мотивы людей вообще, предполагает худшее. Sceptical — просто не убеждён чем-то конкретным, без предположений о злом умысле.

reverse.text: I'm [[sceptical]] about these new diet pills — I'd like to see some real evidence first.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь просто нет убеждённости, нужны доказательства — sceptical. Cynical добавило бы предположение о злом умысле, которого тут нет.

fixIt.text: I'm quite [[sceptical]] about human nature in general — I think everyone secretly acts out of self-interest.
fixIt.explanationRu: Общее недоверие к мотивам людей — cynical. Sceptical — просто «не убеждён», без предположения о плохих намерениях.

wordFormation.text: Even as a teenager, he had a [[cynical]] streak that worried his parents.

reply.context: A friend says: "I think that charity only donates money for the tax break, not because they care."
options: Honestly, that's a pretty cynical way to look at it — I think they do care.
You're so cynical, you always trust everyone's motives completely.
Indeed, one must remain thoroughly cynical regarding all charitable undertakings, my friend.
reply.explanationRu: Cynical — не верить в искренность чужих мотивов; во втором варианте смысл перепутан («доверяет всем» противоречит cynical). Третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: He no longer believes that people do good things for honest reasons.
rewrite.frame: He has become ____ about people's motives.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Разувериться в искренности людей» — become cynical about people's motives.

definitionEn: likely to cause serious harm to someone's health, reputation or interests
situation: News, a habit or a decision could seriously hurt someone's health, reputation or chances of success.

examples.text: The leaked emails were hugely [[damaging]] to the senator's campaign.
Smoking has a well-documented [[damaging]] effect on the lungs.
Losing three clients in one week was hugely [[damaging]] for team morale.

texts: The scandal proved [[damaging]] to the company's reputation.
Too much sun exposure can be [[damaging]] to your skin.
Critics called the new policy economically [[damaging]].

badCollocation.noteRu: После прилагательного damaging нужен предлог to: damaging to your health. Без to — грамматическая ошибка (либо нужен глагол damages).

collocationTask.prompt: The scandal proved hugely ___ to his career.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Damaging — вредный, разрушительный. Reassuring, promising и convenient со скандалом, портящим карьеру, не сочетаются по смыслу.

nuance.text: The report's [[damaging]] revelations forced two ministers to resign.
nuance.explanationRu: Damaging — причиняющий вред (то, что вредит чему-то). Damaged — уже повреждённый, пострадавший сам; a damaged reputation — это результат, а не причина.

reverse.text: After the scandal, his once-solid reputation was badly [[damaged]].
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь репутация сама пострадала — damaged (результат). Damaging описывает то, что причиняет вред, а не то, что уже повреждено.

fixIt.text: His [[damaged]] comments about immigration caused a huge public outcry.
fixIt.explanationRu: Комментарии, которые вредят репутации, — damaging comments. Damaged значит «повреждённый», к высказываниям так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: The lawyer warned that the leaked memo could prove extremely [[damaging]] in court.

reply.context: A colleague whispers: "Did you see what the CEO said to the press about our biggest client?"
options: Yes, it was pretty damaging — I can't believe he said that on record.
Yes, it was really damaging news — investors are absolutely thrilled about it.
Indeed, his remarks shall doubtless prove most damaging to our corporate standing.
reply.explanationRu: Damaging — вредный, разрушительный; инвесторы не радуются «вредным» новостям (ошибка во втором варианте). Третий ответ слишком официален для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The report seriously hurt the company's public image.
rewrite.frame: The report was extremely ____ to the company's public image.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Серьёзно повредил репутации» — was damaging to the company's image.

definitionEn: the moment when a new period, situation or era begins
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «начало новой эпохи» (the dawn of civilization); буквальное «рассвет» (солнце встаёт) не рассматривается.
situation: A completely new age, technology or way of life begins, changing things for a long time afterwards.

examples.text: Scientists call this discovery the [[dawn]] of a new era in medicine.
The invention of the printing press marked the [[dawn]] of mass communication.
Many historians see the steam engine as marking the [[dawn]] of the industrial age.

texts: The fall of the wall seemed to signal the [[dawn]] of a freer Europe.
For many fans, that album marked the [[dawn]] of a new sound in rock music.
Historians often describe the wheel as the [[dawn]] of modern transport.

badCollocation.noteRu: Dawn — про начало долгой эпохи или большого исторического периода, а не короткого события вроде встречи: там просто the start/beginning of the meeting.

collocationTask.prompt: at the ___ of the nuclear age
collocationTask.explanationRu: «На заре» новой эпохи — at the dawn of. Morning, sunrise и noon — про время суток буквально, в этом переносном значении так не говорят.

nuance.text: Historians often speak of the [[dawn]] of the atomic age.
nuance.explanationRu: Dawn в переносном смысле — начало важной эпохи. Sunrise — буквальный восход солнца, к историческим эпохам это слово не применяют.

reverse.text: We got up before [[sunrise]] to watch the hot-air balloons take off.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о буквальном восходе солнца — sunrise. Переносное «начало эпохи» тут не подходит.

fixIt.text: The moon landing marked the [[sunrise]] of the space age.
fixIt.explanationRu: Начало эпохи — the dawn of something (переносное значение). Sunrise — только буквальный восход солнца.

wordFormation.text: There was a slow [[dawning]] realization that the old strategy no longer worked.

definitionEn: to let your mind wander pleasantly instead of paying attention to what you should be doing
situation: Instead of listening or concentrating, your mind drifts off into pleasant thoughts and imagined scenes.

examples.text: Instead of taking notes, he spent the lecture [[daydreaming]] about his holiday.
She often [[daydreams]] about quitting her job and opening a small bakery.
Careful — you'll walk into a lamppost if you keep [[daydreaming]] like that!

texts: He was [[daydreaming]] about the beach when the teacher called his name.
She caught herself [[daydreaming]] again during the budget meeting.
The children sat [[daydreaming]] out of the classroom window.

badCollocation.noteRu: Daydream — просто мечтательно отвлекаться, а не составлять план: продумать план — make/come up with a plan, а не daydream one.

collocationTask.prompt: he spent the whole meeting ___ about his holiday
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Витать в облаках», мечтая, — daydream about something. Complaining, negotiating и apologising не про мечтательную рассеянность.

nuance.text: Instead of finishing his homework, he sat [[daydreaming]] about becoming a famous footballer.
nuance.explanationRu: Daydream — мечтать наяву, отвлекаясь от дел. Dream чаще о снах во время сна или о больших жизненных мечтах вообще; про рассеянность на уроке точнее daydream.

reverse.text: Every night she [[dreamed]] about the same strange house by the sea.
reverse.explanationRu: Речь о снах во время сна — dream. Daydream — только наяву, про сны во время сна так не говорят.

fixIt.text: He spent the whole class [[dreaming]] about lunch instead of listening to the teacher.
fixIt.explanationRu: О рассеянности наяву, на уроке, говорят daydream, а не dream (dream — про сны во время сна).

wordFormation.text: His teachers always said he was a hopeless [[daydreamer]] who never paid attention.

definitionEn: broken pieces of something that has been destroyed or wrecked
senseNote: Здесь — «обломки» после катастрофы, взрыва или крушения; бытовой «мусор» (litter, rubbish) не рассматривается.
situation: After an explosion, storm or crash, broken pieces of buildings, vehicles or objects are scattered around.

examples.text: Rescue workers searched through the [[debris]] for survivors after the earthquake.
Pieces of [[debris]] from the old satellite burned up in the atmosphere.
The storm left [[debris]] scattered across the beach for miles.

texts: Workers spent weeks clearing [[debris]] from the collapsed bridge.
Scientists are tracking a growing cloud of [[debris]] in orbit.
Flood [[debris]] blocked the entrance to the underground car park.

badCollocation.text: throw the [[debris]] in the bin after the party
badCollocation.noteRu: После вечеринки обычную уборку называют rubbish/litter/trash, а не debris. Debris — обломки после разрушения, а не бытовой мусор.

collocationTask.prompt: rescue teams searched the ___ for survivors
collocationTask.explanationRu: После крушения ищут среди обломков — search the debris. Luggage, paperwork и inventory по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: The explosion scattered [[debris]] across three city blocks.
nuance.explanationRu: Debris — обломки после разрушения (взрыва, аварии). Litter — обычный бытовой мусор (обёртки, бутылки), для взрыва это слово не подходит.

reverse.text: Volunteers picked up [[litter]] along the riverbank every Sunday morning.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь обычный бытовой мусор — litter. Debris — именно обломки чего-то разрушенного, для обёрток и бутылок так не говорят.

fixIt.text: After the storm, workers spent days clearing [[litter]] from the collapsed roofs and broken fences.
fixIt.explanationRu: Обломки крыш и заборов после урагана — debris. Litter — обычный мусор, а не обломки разрушений.

definitionEn: the first public performance or appearance of someone or something
situation: A performer, athlete or product appears in public or on the market for the very first time.

examples.text: The young violinist made her [[debut]] with the city orchestra last night.
The company's new electric car will make its [[debut]] at the motor show.
His acting [[debut]] earned him surprisingly good reviews.

texts: The striker scored twice on his international [[debut]].
Her first novel marked a stunning literary [[debut]].
The band's [[debut]] sold out within an hour.

badCollocation.noteRu: Debut не «делают» (do): его make — make your debut, а не do a debut.

collocationTask.prompt: he made his professional ___ at just seventeen
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Дебютировать» — make your debut. Retirement, résumé и apprenticeship по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: The young pianist made a remarkable [[debut]] at the age of sixteen.
nuance.explanationRu: Debut — первое выступление человека (пианиста, актёра). Premiere — первый показ произведения (фильма, спектакля), а не выступление самого человека.

reverse.text: The restored classic will have its [[premiere]] screening at the London Film Festival this year.
reverse.explanationRu: Показ уже существующего старого фильма — premiere. Debut — только про первое выступление или первую работу автора.

fixIt.text: The young gymnast's outstanding [[premiere]] at the national championships surprised everyone.
fixIt.explanationRu: Первое выступление человека — debut, а не premiere (premiere — первый показ фильма или спектакля).

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was your sister's first violin recital last night?"
options: It went really well — quite an impressive debut, actually.
It went well — she's planning her debut retirement party next year too.
One is given to understand that her inaugural recital proceeded most satisfactorily.
reply.explanationRu: Debut — первое выступление, а не «уход на покой» (отсюда странность второго варианта). Третий звучит слишком архаично для ответа другу.

rewrite.original: The actress performed on stage for the very first time last night.
rewrite.frame: The actress made her ____ on stage last night.

definitionEn: dishonest behaviour intended to make someone believe something false
situation: Someone deliberately hides the truth or creates a false impression in order to trick another person.

examples.text: Their marriage was built on years of [[deceit]] and hidden debts.
The journalist uncovered a web of corporate [[deceit]] behind the merger.
She felt sick with guilt at her own small act of [[deceit]].

texts: He was shocked by the sheer scale of her [[deceit]].
Years of [[deceit]] finally destroyed their friendship.
The novel explores love, betrayal and [[deceit]] in equal measure.

badCollocation.text: tell a [[deceit]] to protect her feelings
badCollocation.noteRu: Deceit — неисчисляемое, сам обман как явление, а не отдельная ложь: одну ложь называют a lie, а не a deceit.

collocationTask.prompt: the scandal revealed a whole web of ___
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Клубок обмана» — a web of deceit, устойчивое сочетание. Charity, diplomacy и curiosity по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: Their whole relationship was based on [[deceit]] rather than trust.
nuance.explanationRu: Deceit — обман как явление или черта характера в целом (неисчисляемое). Lies — конкретные, отдельные ложные высказывания; здесь речь именно об общем характере отношений.

reverse.text: He told so many [[lies]] that she stopped believing anything he said.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь конкретные, повторяющиеся ложные высказывания — lies. Deceit — само явление обмана в целом, а не отдельные высказывания.

fixIt.text: Their entire relationship, she realised, had been built on his constant [[fraud]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Fraud — конкретное юридическое мошенничество, обычно финансовое. Обман в личных отношениях, как общее явление, — deceit.

wordFormation.text: After years of secrecy, the full extent of his [[deceit]] finally came out.

reply.context: A friend says: "I just found out my business partner has been hiding the real accounts from me for years."
options: That's awful — that kind of deceit can destroy a business overnight.
That's awful — I'm sure it was just an honest mix-up, not deceit at all.
One can only lament such duplicitous conduct on the part of your associate.
reply.explanationRu: Ситуация описывает намеренный обман, поэтому «not deceit at all» во втором варианте противоречит фактам. Третий ответ звучит слишком книжно для разговора с другом.
